questions.question: A coil has a resistance of 44 Omega . If it is connected across a 220 {V} supply, what is the power consumed by the coil?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Power formula**: The power consumed by a resistor is calculated using the formula **P = V² / R**, where **P** is the power, **V** is the voltage, and **R** is the resistance.
 
• **Given values**: In the question, the resistance of the coil is **44 Ω**, and the voltage applied across it is **220 V**.
 
• **Substitute the values**: Substituting these values into the formula:

 **P = (220)² / 44**
 
• **Calculation**:

 **(220)² = 48400**

 **P = 48400 / 44 = 1100 W**.
 
• **Result**: The power consumed by the coil is **1100 W**, which corresponds to Option 3__.
 
• This calculation aligns with the question, confirming that the **correct answer is 1100 W**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Ohm's Law:**

 
 
• Ohm's Law states that **V = IR**, where **V** is voltage, **I** is current, and **R** is resistance.
 
• This law is fundamental in analyzing electrical circuits and understanding the relationship between voltage, current, and resistance.
 
 
 
• **Power in Electrical Circuits:**
 
 
• Power in an electrical circuit is the rate at which energy is consumed or converted.
 
• The formula **P = V² / R** is derived by combining Ohm's Law and the general power formula **P = VI**.
 
• It highlights the quadratic relationship between voltage and power for a fixed resistance.
 
 
 
• **Units of Measurement:**
 
 
• **Voltage:** Measured in **Volts (V)**.
 
• **Resistance:** Measured in **Ohms (Ω)**.
 
• **Power:** Measured in **Watts (W)**.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Power Formula:**
 
 
• This formula is critical in designing electrical appliances, ensuring optimal performance without overheating.
 
• It is also used in estimating energy consumption for billing purposes in residential, commercial, and industrial sectors.
 
 
 
• **Resistive Load:**
 
 
• The coil in the question behaves as a resistive load, where the power calculation does not involve reactive components like inductance or capacitance.
 
• This simplifies the calculation to a purely resistive scenario.

questions.question: The functional group which does NOT contain oxygen hetero atom is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**halo alkane**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **functional group** is a specific group of atoms within a molecule that is responsible for characteristic chemical reactions of that molecule.
 
• The options in the question refer to different types of **functional groups**: **alcohols, halo alkanes, ketones, and carboxylic acids.**
 
• **Halo alkane** (also known as alkyl halide) does not contain oxygen in its structure. It consists of a carbon atom bonded to a halogen atom (fluorine, chlorine, bromine, or iodine).
 
• All other options (alcohol, ketone, carboxylic acid) contain oxygen as part of their functional groups:
 
 
• **Alcohol**: Contains an -OH group.
 
• **Ketone**: Contains a carbonyl group (C=O).
 
• **Carboxylic acid**: Contains a carboxyl group (-COOH).
 
 
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **halo alkane**__, as it is the only functional group that does not contain oxygen.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Alcohols:**

 
 
• Alcohols are organic compounds with one or more hydroxyl (-OH) groups attached to a carbon atom.
 
• General formula: **R-OH**, where R is an alkyl group.
 
• They are commonly used in beverages, antiseptics, and as industrial solvents.
 
 
 
• **Halo alkanes:**
 
 
• Also called alkyl halides, they are compounds in which one or more hydrogen atoms in an alkane are replaced by halogen atoms (F, Cl, Br, or I).
 
• General formula: **R-X**, where R is an alkyl group and X is a halogen.
 
• They are used in refrigerants, solvents, and as intermediates in chemical synthesis.
 
 
 
• **Ketones:**
 
 
• Ketones contain a carbonyl group (C=O) bonded to two carbon atoms.
 
• General formula: **R-CO-R'**, where R and R' are alkyl or aryl groups.
 
• Common example: Acetone (propanone), which is widely used as a solvent and in nail polish remover.
 
 
 
• **Carboxylic Acids:**
 
 
• These are organic acids containing a carboxyl group (-COOH).
 
• General formula: **R-COOH**, where R is an alkyl or aryl group.
 
• They are found in substances like vinegar (acetic acid) and are used in food, pharmaceuticals, and industrial processes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Halo alkanes' Characteristics:**

 
 
• Halo alkanes are classified based on the type of halogen atom and the degree of substitution (primary, secondary, or tertiary).
 
• They undergo reactions like **nucleophilic substitution** and **elimination**, making them versatile in organic synthesis.
 
 
 
• **Functional Groups in Chemistry:**
 
 
• Functional groups determine the chemical properties and reactivity of organic compounds.
 
• They serve as the basis for naming and classifying organic compounds in IUPAC nomenclature.

questions.question: Which of the following options best describes the term Culture Fishery?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Farming of the fishes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Culture Fishery** refers to the **controlled farming of fish**, where the growth and production of fish are enhanced by human intervention in a controlled environment such as ponds, tanks, or other artificial water bodies.
 
• The primary purpose of culture fishery is to **increase fish production** to meet the demand for seafood and to provide a source of livelihood to individuals engaged in aquaculture.
 
• This type of fishery involves techniques such as **breeding, rearing, and harvesting of fish** in artificial or semi-natural water bodies.
 
• Culture fishery is a part of **aquaculture**, which also includes farming of other aquatic organisms like crustaceans, mollusks, and aquatic plants.
 
• It plays a critical role in **sustainable fish production**, ensuring a consistent supply of fish while reducing pressure on natural water bodies and marine ecosystems.
 
• Examples of fish species commonly used in culture fishery include **Rohu, Catla, Mrigal, Tilapia, and Carp**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Fisheries:**

 
 
• **Capture Fishery:** This involves the harvesting of fish from their natural habitats, such as rivers, lakes, and oceans. It does not involve human intervention in the breeding or rearing of fish.
 
• **Culture Fishery:** This involves the farming of fish in controlled environments like ponds, tanks, or reservoirs, where humans control the conditions for fish growth and reproduction.
 
• **Marine Fishery:** This type of fishery deals with the capture or farming of fish in marine ecosystems, such as oceans and seas.
 
• **Inland Fishery:** This involves the capture and farming of fish in freshwater ecosystems like rivers, lakes, and reservoirs.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Culture Fishery:**
 
 
• It contributes significantly to **food security** by providing a consistent supply of fish protein.
 
• It supports the **economy** by creating livelihood opportunities for farmers and workers in the aquaculture sector.
 
• Culture fishery reduces **overfishing** in natural water bodies, helping to conserve marine biodiversity.
 
• It allows for the production of **high-value fish species** that are in demand in domestic and international markets.
 
 
 
• **Features of Culture Fishery:**
 
 
• It involves the use of **scientific techniques** to monitor water quality, feed quality, and fish health.
 
• Fish farming systems can be classified into **extensive, semi-intensive, and intensive systems** based on the level of human intervention and stocking density.
 
• It often includes practices like **polyculture** (culturing multiple species in the same water body) to optimize resource use and enhance productivity.
 
 
 
• **India’s Role in Aquaculture:**
 
 
• India is one of the leading producers of fish through aquaculture, ranking **second globally** after China.
 
• Key states involved in culture fisheries include **Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal, Odisha, and Kerala**.
 
• The government promotes aquaculture through initiatives like the **Blue Revolution Scheme** and the **Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY)**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Comparison of Capture and Culture Fisheries:**

 
 
• **Capture Fisheries:** Depend on wild fish populations and are subject to environmental factors and overfishing.
 
• **Culture Fisheries:** Provide controlled conditions for fish farming, ensuring consistent yields and reduced environmental impact.
 
 
 
• **Key Challenges in Culture Fishery:**
 
 
• Maintaining **water quality** and controlling diseases in fish farms.
 
• Ensuring the availability of **quality fish feed** and seeds for farming.
 
• Addressing environmental concerns, such as **water pollution** and the ecological impact of intensive aquaculture practices.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT used for expressing the concentration of a solution?

options.text: Volume by Volume percentage of a solution
Mass by volume percentage of a solution
Volume by Mass percentage of a solution
Mass by mass percentage of a solution

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Volume by Mass percentage of a solution**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Volume by Volume percentage (v/v%)**: This is a common way to express the concentration of a solution, particularly for liquids. It is calculated as the volume of the solute divided by the total volume of the solution, multiplied by 100. **Example:** Alcohol in water solutions.
 
• **Mass by Volume percentage (m/v%)**: This is a widely used method in laboratories and industries. It represents the mass of the solute in grams per 100 mL of the solution. **Example:** Saline solution (NaCl in water).
 
• **Volume by Mass percentage (v/m%)**: This method is **not commonly used** for expressing the concentration of a solution, as it does not align with standard practices in chemistry. This inconsistency in units makes it impractical and rarely adopted.
 
• **Mass by Mass percentage (m/m%)**: This is another standard way to express concentration. It is the mass of the solute divided by the total mass of the solution, multiplied by 100. **Example:** Sugar in water solutions.
 
• The correct answer is **Volume by Mass percentage**, as it is not a standard method for expressing the concentration of a solution in scientific or industrial contexts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Concentration of a solution:** It refers to the amount of solute that is dissolved in a given quantity of solvent. It is usually expressed as a percentage or in molarity, molality, or normality.
 
• **Molarity (M):** It is the number of moles of solute per liter of solution. It is one of the most commonly used units of concentration in chemistry. **Example:** 1 M NaOH solution contains 1 mole of NaOH per liter of solution.
 
• **Molality (m):** It is the number of moles of solute per kilogram of solvent. Unlike molarity, it is not affected by temperature changes as it depends on mass rather than volume.
 
• **Normality (N):** It is the number of gram-equivalents of solute per liter of solution. It is often used in acid-base reactions and redox reactions.
 
• **Parts per Million (ppm):** It is a unit of concentration used for very dilute solutions, representing the number of parts of solute per million parts of solution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Applications of concentration expressions:**

 
 
• **Volume by Volume percentage:** Commonly used in industries like alcoholic beverages and cosmetics.
 
• **Mass by Volume percentage:** Frequently utilized in pharmaceutical preparations and clinical solutions like glucose solutions or saline.
 
• **Mass by Mass percentage:** Used in food and chemical industries for solid mixtures.
 
 
 
• **Importance of standardization:** The use of standardized units like molarity, molality, and percentage ensures uniformity in scientific communication and industrial processes.
 
• **Practicality in laboratory settings:** Units like molarity and mass by volume percentage are preferred due to ease of measurement and preparation of solutions.

questions.question: Which of the following plant tissue performs photosynthesis?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chlorenchyma**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Chlorenchyma** is a type of parenchyma tissue in plants that contains chloroplasts, which are essential for the process of **photosynthesis**.
 
• This tissue is primarily found in the **mesophyll layer of leaves** and in green stems, where it plays a crucial role in **capturing sunlight** and synthesizing food.
 
• The chloroplasts in chlorenchyma cells contain **chlorophyll**, the pigment responsible for absorbing light energy and converting it into chemical energy.
 
• In addition to photosynthesis, chlorenchyma also contributes to **gaseous exchange** and stores the products of photosynthesis temporarily.
 
• Unlike other plant tissues like sclerenchyma, xylem, or phloem, chlorenchyma is a living tissue that remains metabolically active and supports the plant’s growth and development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sclerenchyma:**

 
 
• Sclerenchyma is a type of plant tissue composed of dead cells with thickened, lignified walls.
 
• It provides **mechanical support** and rigidity to the plant but does not participate in photosynthesis.
 
• Examples include fibers and sclereids, which are found in hard parts of the plant, such as seed coats and nutshells.
 
 
 
• **Phloem:**
 
 
• Phloem is a vascular tissue responsible for the **transport of food** (mainly sucrose) in plants from the leaves to other parts of the plant.
 
• It consists of sieve elements, companion cells, phloem fibers, and phloem parenchyma.
 
• Although phloem is vital for the distribution of photosynthetic products, it does not perform photosynthesis itself.
 
 
 
• **Xylem:**
 
 
• Xylem is another vascular tissue that primarily functions in the **transport of water and minerals** from roots to leaves.
 
• It is composed of tracheids, vessels, xylem fibers, and xylem parenchyma.
 
• Similar to phloem, xylem does not carry out photosynthesis.
 
 
 
• **Parenchyma:**
 
 
• Parenchyma is a versatile plant tissue that performs various functions, such as storage, secretion, and photosynthesis (in the case of chlorenchyma).
 
• It is characterized by thin cell walls and large intercellular spaces, which allow efficient exchange of gases and nutrients.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Photosynthesis:**

 
 
• Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants convert light energy into chemical energy in the form of glucose.
 
• This process occurs in the chloroplasts, which contain the pigment **chlorophyll**.
 
• The general equation for photosynthesis is:

 Carbon dioxide + Water + Sunlight → Glucose + Oxygen
 
 
 
• **Chloroplast:**
 
 
• Chloroplasts are specialized organelles found in plant cells and some algae that are responsible for photosynthesis.
 
• They have a double membrane structure and contain **thylakoids**, where the light-dependent reactions occur, and the **stroma**, where the Calvin cycle takes place.
 
 
 
• **Role of Chlorenchyma in Plants:**
 
 
• Chlorenchyma not only aids in photosynthesis but also contributes to **gas exchange** and **water regulation** in leaves.
 
• It ensures that the plant has a steady supply of energy for growth, reproduction, and other physiological processes.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: Work done can only be positive.
Work done can be positive or negative depending on the direction of force.
Work done does not depend on force or displacement.
Work done can only be negative.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Work done can be positive or negative depending on the direction of force**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Work Done:** Work is the measure of energy transfer that occurs when an object is moved over a distance by an external force. The formula for work is **W = F × d × cos(θ)**, where **F** is the force, **d** is the displacement, and **θ** is the angle between the force and displacement.
 
• **Positive Work:** Work is considered positive when the force applied and the displacement of the object are in the same direction. For example, lifting an object upward where the applied force and displacement are both upward.
 
• **Negative Work:** Work is negative when the force is applied in the opposite direction to the displacement. For instance, when friction acts against the motion of an object sliding on a surface.
 
• **Dependence on Force and Displacement:** Work depends on the magnitude of the force, the displacement of the object, and the angle between them. If either force or displacement is zero, no work is done.
 
• **Direction of Force:** The sign of work depends on the angle **θ**. If **θ** is less than 90°, work is positive; if **θ** is greater than 90°, work is negative. If **θ = 90°**, no work is done as the force is perpendicular to displacement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Work Done in Everyday Life:**

 
 
• When you push a cart forward, positive work is done as the force and displacement are in the same direction.
 
• While stopping a moving car, the brakes do negative work as the frictional force opposes the motion of the car.
 
 
 
• **Work Done in Physics:**
 
 
• Work is a scalar quantity, meaning it has magnitude but no direction.
 
• Units of work include the **joule (J)** in the SI system and the **erg** in the CGS system.
 
 
 
• **Zero Work:**
 
 
• Work becomes zero when there is no displacement, or the force is perpendicular to the displacement (e.g., carrying a bag horizontally).
 
• In circular motion, when centripetal force acts perpendicular to the displacement, no work is done.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Work:**
 
 
• In engineering, work is used to calculate energy transfer in machines.
 
• In biomechanics, it measures the work done by muscles during physical activity.
 
 
 
• **Important Formulae and Concepts:**
 
 
• **W = F × d × cos(θ)**: Main formula for calculating work.
 
• **Positive Work:** When force and displacement are in the same direction (**θ = 0°**).
 
• **Negative Work:** When force and displacement are in opposite directions (**θ = 180°**).
 
• **Zero Work:** When **θ = 90°** or **F = 0** or **d = 0**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Statement Analysis:**

 
 
• **Statement 1:** "Work done can only be positive." This is incorrect, as work can also be negative depending on the direction of force and displacement.
 
• **Statement 2:** "Work done can be positive or negative depending on the direction of force." This is correct, as explained above.
 
• **Statement 3:** "Work done does not depend on force or displacement." This is incorrect because work depends directly on both force and displacement.
 
• **Statement 4:** "Work done can only be negative." This is incorrect, as work can also be positive.

questions.question: Which of the following statements best explains the Law of Constant Proportions?

options.text: A chemical compound always contains the same elements in the same proportion by mass.
Elements are always found in random ratios in a compound.
Mass can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction.
Atoms can be divided into smaller particles during a reaction.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A chemical compound always contains the same elements in the same proportion by mass.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Law of Constant Proportions**, also known as the **Law of Definite Proportions**, states that a given chemical compound always contains its constituent elements in a **fixed ratio by mass**, regardless of the source or how it was prepared.
 
• This law was proposed by **Joseph Proust** in **1794** and is fundamental to the study of chemistry.
 
• For example, water (H₂O) is always composed of hydrogen and oxygen in a mass ratio of approximately **1:8**, irrespective of its origin—whether it comes from a river, ocean, or laboratory.
 
• It demonstrates that the composition of a compound is always **uniform and consistent**, which is essential for chemical reactions and stoichiometry.
 
• The law applies to **pure chemical compounds** and does not hold for mixtures, where the composition can vary.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Understanding the Options:**

 
 
• **Option 1:** "A chemical compound always contains the same elements in the same proportion by mass." This is the correct explanation of the **Law of Constant Proportions**.
 
• **Option 2:** "Elements are always found in random ratios in a compound." This is **false**, as elements combine in specific ratios to form compounds, as per the law.
 
• **Option 3:** "Mass can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction." This is the **Law of Conservation of Mass**, not the Law of Constant Proportions.
 
• **Option 4:** "Atoms can be divided into smaller particles during a reaction." This statement is **false**, as chemical reactions involve the rearrangement of atoms, not their division. The division of atoms occurs only in nuclear reactions.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Law:**
 
 
• The Law of Constant Proportions is crucial for determining the **empirical formula** and **molecular formula** of compounds.
 
• It provides the foundation for understanding the **quantitative relationships** in chemical reactions (stoichiometry).
 
 
 
• **Exceptions to the Law:**
 
 
• It does not apply to compounds with **non-stoichiometric compositions**, such as metal oxides (e.g., FeO).
 
• Isotopic variations of elements can slightly alter the mass ratios in some cases.
 
 
 
• **Related Laws in Chemistry:**
 
 
• **Law of Conservation of Mass:** Proposed by **Antoine Lavoisier**, it states that mass is neither created nor destroyed in chemical reactions.
 
• **Law of Multiple Proportions:** Proposed by **John Dalton**, it states that when two elements form more than one compound, the ratios of the masses of one element that combine with a fixed mass of the other are in small whole numbers.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Law of Constant Proportions** is applicable to **pure chemical compounds** only and not to mixtures.
 
• It is a fundamental principle used in determining the **purity** of chemical substances.
 
• The law supports **atomic theory**, which states that compounds are formed by the combination of atoms in fixed ratios.
 
• This law is used extensively in industries like **pharmaceuticals** and **chemical manufacturing** to ensure product consistency.

questions.question: What is the main role of micelles in the cleansing action of soap?

options.text: To reduce the hardness of water
To increase the surface tension of water
To trap and remove oil and dirt from clothes

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To trap and remove oil and dirt from clothes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Micelles** are aggregates of soap molecules formed when soap is dissolved in water. These molecules are made up of two parts: a hydrophilic (water-attracting) head and a hydrophobic (water-repelling) tail.
 
• The hydrophobic tails of soap molecules attach to grease, oil, or dirt particles, while the hydrophilic heads remain in water. This forms a structure called a **micelle**, where the dirt or grease is trapped inside.
 
• When water is rinsed, these micelles, containing dirt and grease, are washed away, effectively cleaning the surface or fabric.
 
• This process is the primary mechanism by which soaps clean clothes, utensils, and skin. It is particularly effective in breaking down non-polar substances like grease and oil, which are otherwise insoluble in water.
 
• Soap’s ability to form micelles makes it a crucial cleaning agent in both household and industrial applications.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Formation of Micelles:**

 
 
• Micelles form when the concentration of soap molecules reaches a critical point called the **critical micelle concentration (CMC)**.
 
• At this concentration, the soap molecules aggregate in such a way that their hydrophobic tails are shielded from water while their hydrophilic heads remain exposed to water.
 
 
 
• **Structure of Soap Molecules:**
 
 
• Soap molecules are long-chain fatty acid salts, typically sodium or potassium salts of fatty acids.
 
• The hydrophobic tail is a long hydrocarbon chain, while the hydrophilic head is an ionic group, such as a carboxylate ion (COO⁻).
 
 
 
• **Role of Soap in Hard Water:**
 
 
• Hard water contains calcium and magnesium ions, which can react with soap to form insoluble scum.
 
• Despite this limitation, soaps are still effective cleaners in soft water or when used with certain additives to counteract hardness.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Micelle Formation:**
 
 
• Besides cleaning, micelle formation is used in various industries, including pharmaceuticals, where micelles are used to deliver hydrophobic drugs in aqueous solutions.
 
• Micelles are also studied in nanotechnology for their potential in targeted drug delivery systems.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Option 1:** "To reduce the hardness of water" is incorrect as soap does not reduce water hardness; instead, it reacts with the ions in hard water to form scum.
 
• **Option 2:** "To increase the surface tension of water" is incorrect because soap reduces the surface tension of water, allowing it to spread and penetrate surfaces more effectively.

questions.question: Through which method of cell division are the diploid chromosomes divided into haploid gametes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Meiosis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Meiosis** is a type of cell division that reduces the chromosome number by half, producing four haploid gametes from one diploid parent cell.
 
• It is essential for sexual reproduction as it ensures the maintenance of the **chromosome number across generations**.
 
• Meiosis occurs in two stages: **Meiosis I** and **Meiosis II**. Meiosis I includes reduction division, where homologous chromosomes are separated, while Meiosis II resembles mitosis.
 
• During meiosis, processes like **crossing over** and **independent assortment** introduce genetic variation, which is crucial for evolution.
 
• Haploid gametes produced by meiosis (e.g., sperm and egg cells in animals, pollen and ovules in plants) combine during fertilization to form a diploid zygote.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Amitosis**:

 
 
• Amitosis is a simple form of cell division that occurs without spindle formation or chromosome condensation.
 
• It is found in some unicellular organisms and involves direct splitting of the nucleus and cytoplasm.
 
• Unlike meiosis, it does not produce haploid gametes or ensure genetic variation.
 
 
 
• **Mitosis**:
 
 
• Mitosis is a type of cell division resulting in two genetically identical diploid daughter cells.
 
• It occurs during growth, repair, and asexual reproduction, but does not produce haploid gametes.
 
• Mitosis is crucial for maintaining genetic stability within an organism.
 
 
 
• **Binary Fission**:
 
 
• Binary fission is a mode of asexual reproduction found in prokaryotes like bacteria.
 
• It involves the replication of genetic material followed by division into two identical daughter cells.
 
• This process does not involve meiosis or the production of haploid gametes.
 
 
 
• **Genetic Variation in Meiosis**:
 
 
• Crossing over occurs during Prophase I, where homologous chromosomes exchange genetic material, creating unique combinations.
 
• Independent assortment in Metaphase I ensures that chromosomes are distributed randomly to gametes.
 
• These mechanisms increase diversity within a population, contributing to adaptation and evolution.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Chromosome Number:** In humans, meiosis reduces the chromosome number from **46 (diploid)** to **23 (haploid)**.
 
• **Stages of Meiosis:** Meiosis I includes Prophase I, Metaphase I, Anaphase I, and Telophase I, while Meiosis II includes similar phases resembling mitosis.
 
• **Applications of Meiosis:** It is essential for gametogenesis (sperm and egg production) and contributes to genetic diversity in sexually reproducing organisms.
 
• **Evolutionary Significance:** Genetic variation introduced by meiosis plays a vital role in the survival of species in changing environments.

questions.question: Which of the following metals is extracted in the middle of the activity series?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Iron**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Iron** is located in the middle of the activity series of metals. The activity series ranks metals based on their reactivity with water, acids, and other substances.
 
• Iron is neither highly reactive like sodium and potassium nor unreactive like gold. It shows moderate reactivity, making it a middle-series metal.
 
• Metals in the middle of the activity series, such as iron, zinc, and lead, are usually extracted from their ores through reduction processes, often using carbon or carbon monoxide as a reducing agent.
 
• The activity series helps determine the method of extraction for different metals. For example, metals high in the series (e.g., sodium, potassium) are extracted via electrolysis, while middle-series metals (e.g., iron) are extracted using smelting or reduction techniques.
 
• Iron’s moderate reactivity makes it a widely used metal in construction, manufacturing, and various industries. Its ores, such as hematite and magnetite, are abundant and economically viable for extraction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Activity Series of Metals:**

 
 
• The activity series is a list of metals arranged in order of decreasing reactivity. Highly reactive metals like potassium and sodium are at the top, while less reactive metals like gold and platinum are at the bottom.
 
• The series is crucial for understanding how metals react with substances like water, acids, and oxygen. It also determines the method of extraction of metals from their ores.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of Metals in the Middle of the Activity Series:**
 
 
• These metals, including iron, zinc, and lead, are moderately reactive. They do not react as vigorously with water or acids as metals at the top of the activity series.
 
• They are usually extracted from their ores through reduction using carbon, as they are not reactive enough to require electrolysis.
 
• Iron is extracted from ores such as hematite (Fe2O3) and magnetite (Fe3O4) in a blast furnace. The process involves reduction with carbon monoxide to produce iron.
 
 
 
• **Specific Characteristics of the Options:**
 
 
• **Sodium and Potassium:** Highly reactive metals found at the top of the activity series. They are extracted via electrolysis of their molten salts.
 
• **Gold:** A noble metal with very low reactivity, found at the bottom of the activity series. It is typically found in its native state in nature and does not require extensive extraction processes.
 
• **Iron:** A metal in the middle of the activity series, extracted using reduction methods such as smelting. It is widely used in construction, tools, and machinery.
 
 
 
• **Important Facts About Iron:**
 
 
• Iron is the fourth most abundant element in the Earth's crust.
 
• It is primarily extracted from hematite and magnetite ores through the blast furnace process.
 
• Iron is a key component in the production of steel, which is essential for construction and industrial purposes.
 
• It is prone to corrosion (rusting) when exposed to moisture and oxygen, but this can be prevented through processes like galvanization or painting.

questions.question: Which of the following describes an example of uniform circular motion?

options.text: A fan blade rotating at constant speed
A car accelerating on its way
A train moving on its track

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A fan blade rotating at constant speed**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Uniform Circular Motion (UCM):** It refers to the motion of an object in a circular path with a constant speed. Although the speed remains constant, the direction of velocity changes continuously, resulting in acceleration known as centripetal acceleration.
 
• **A fan blade rotating at constant speed:** The fan blade undergoes uniform circular motion because each point on the blade moves along a circular path at a constant speed, with centripetal force acting towards the center of the fan. ***This is the correct example of UCM.***
 
• **A ball thrown vertically upwards:** This motion is linear (not circular) and is influenced by gravitational force, causing the ball to decelerate while moving up and accelerate while coming down. ***Hence, this is not an example of UCM.***
 
• **A car accelerating on its way:** The car’s motion is typically along a straight or curved path with changing speed and direction. Both the velocity and acceleration change, making it non-uniform motion. ***This is not an example of UCM.***
 
• **A train moving on its track:** Unless specified that the train is moving in a circular path at constant speed, this is generally linear motion. ***Hence, this is not an example of UCM.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Characteristics of Uniform Circular Motion (UCM):**

 
 
• **Constant Speed:** The magnitude of velocity remains unchanged throughout the motion.
 
• **Changing Velocity Direction:** Since the object is moving in a circle, the direction of velocity changes continuously.
 
• **Centripetal Acceleration:** The acceleration is directed towards the center of the circle and is responsible for changing the direction of velocity.
 
• **Centripetal Force:** The force that keeps the object in circular motion acts towards the center of the circle.
 
• **Examples:** A satellite orbiting Earth, a stone tied to a string and whirled in a circle, and planets revolving around the Sun.
 
 
 
• **Non-Uniform Circular Motion:**
 
 
• If the speed of the object moving in a circular path changes, it is called non-uniform circular motion.
 
• In this case, both tangential acceleration (due to changing speed) and centripetal acceleration (due to changing direction) are present.
 
 
 
• **Difference Between Uniform and Non-Uniform Circular Motion:**
 
 
• **Uniform Circular Motion:** Constant speed with changing velocity direction; only centripetal acceleration is present.
 
• **Non-Uniform Circular Motion:** Changing speed and direction of velocity; both centripetal and tangential accelerations are present.
 
 
 
• **Applications of UCM:**
 
 
• **Artificial Satellites:** Satellites revolve around Earth in uniform circular motion under the influence of gravitational force.
 
• **Vehicle Turns:** Vehicles negotiating circular turns demonstrate the concept of centripetal force.
 
• **Amusement Rides:** Many rides in amusement parks use uniform circular motion principles to ensure thrilling yet safe experiences.

questions.question: A body is dropped from a height. If it falls for 3.0 s and g = 10 {m/s}² , its final velocity (v) is ______________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2 (30 m/s)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Final velocity (v) of a freely falling body** can be calculated using the formula: **v = u + g × t**, where:

 
 
• **u** is the initial velocity of the body (0 m/s for a body dropped from rest).
 
• **g** is the acceleration due to gravity (10 m/s² in this case).
 
• **t** is the time for which the body falls (3.0 seconds).
 
 
 
• Substituting the values into the formula:
 
 
• v = 0 + (10 × 3) = 30 m/s.
 
 
 
• **Final velocity v = 30 m/s**, which matches Option 2__.
 
• This calculation assumes no air resistance, meaning the motion occurs in a vacuum or idealized free fall conditions.
 
• The result directly demonstrates the effect of uniform acceleration due to gravity on a freely falling object.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Equations of motion:**

 
 
• These equations describe the motion of objects under constant acceleration. The three primary equations are:
 
 
• v = u + a × t
 
• s = u × t + 0.5 × a × t²
 
• v² = u² + 2 × a × s
 
 
 
• In this case, the first equation is used as the distance (s) is not required.
 
 
 
• **Free fall:**
 
 
• When an object falls under the influence of gravity alone, it is said to be in free fall.
 
• During free fall, the acceleration of the object is equal to the acceleration due to gravity (g ≈ 9.8 m/s² or 10 m/s² for approximation).
 
 
 
• **Initial velocity (u):**
 
 
• If an object is dropped (not thrown), its initial velocity is 0 m/s.
 
 
 
• **Factors affecting free fall:**
 
 
• Free fall neglects air resistance; if air resistance is considered, the motion becomes non-uniform.
 
• In reality, objects with different shapes and masses may fall at different rates due to air drag, even though gravity affects all objects equally.
 
 
 
• **Applications of free fall:**
 
 
• Understanding free fall is essential in physics and engineering, such as designing parachutes or calculating projectile motion.

questions.question: The motion of a satellite orbiting the Earth in a circular path at constant speed is a classic example of uniform circular motion. What property of this motion prevents its acceleration from being zero?

options.text: The direction of motion changes continuously at every point, meaning the velocity is changing.
The total mechanical energy is conserved, necessitating acceleration.
The speed is too high for the gravitational force to sustain a constant velocity.
The object`s mass continually changes due to orbital dynamics.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The direction of motion changes continuously at every point, meaning the velocity is changing.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Uniform circular motion** refers to the motion of an object moving in a circular path at a constant speed.
 
• Even though the **speed remains constant**, the **direction of motion** changes continuously as the object moves along the circular path. This results in a change in the velocity vector.
 
• Acceleration in circular motion is caused by this continuous change in the direction of the velocity vector, even when the magnitude of velocity (speed) remains constant. This acceleration is known as **centripetal acceleration**.
 
• **Centripetal acceleration** acts towards the center of the circle, ensuring the object stays on the circular path. Without this acceleration, the object would move tangentially to the circle due to inertia.
 
• Thus, the motion cannot have zero acceleration, as the continuous change in direction of motion inherently necessitates acceleration. *Hence, the statement is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option Analysis:

 
 
• Option 1: Correct. The direction of motion changes continuously, causing velocity to change and necessitating acceleration.
 
• Option 2: Incorrect. Conservation of total mechanical energy does not directly imply acceleration; it refers to the sum of kinetic and potential energy being constant.
 
• Option 3: Incorrect. The speed is sustained by the balance between gravitational force and centripetal force, not because of high speed alone.
 
• Option 4: Incorrect. The mass of a satellite does not change significantly during circular motion.
 
 
 
• **Properties of Uniform Circular Motion:**
 
 
• The motion is characterized by a constant speed but a continuously changing velocity due to directional changes.
 
• The force responsible for maintaining circular motion is called **centripetal force**, directed towards the center of the circle.
 
• Examples of such motion include the **orbit of planets**, **motion of satellites**, and **vehicles turning on a circular track**.
 
 
 
• **Centripetal Force and Acceleration:**
 
 
• **Centripetal acceleration** is calculated using the formula **a = v²/r**, where **v** is the speed and **r** is the radius of the circular path.
 
• This acceleration is perpendicular to the velocity and is responsible for changing the direction of the object’s motion.
 
• Common sources of centripetal force include **gravitational force** in planetary motion and **frictional force** in vehicle turns.
 
 
 
• **Misconceptions about Circular Motion:**
 
 
• It is often incorrectly assumed that there is no acceleration in uniform circular motion because the speed is constant. However, acceleration exists due to the continuous change in direction.
 
• Acceleration does not imply an increase in speed; it can also mean a change in the direction of velocity.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Circular Motion:**
 
 
• Used in designing **centrifugal pumps**, **roller coasters**, and **rotating machinery**.
 
• Helps in understanding the behavior of **celestial bodies** like planets and satellites.
 
• Critical for analyzing the motion of vehicles on **curved roads** or tracks.

questions.question: The fractional atomic mass of chlorine is due to which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Presence of isotopes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The fractional atomic mass of **chlorine** arises due to the **presence of isotopes**, which are atoms of the same element with the same number of protons but a different number of neutrons.
 
• Chlorine primarily exists as two naturally occurring isotopes: **Chlorine-35 (35Cl)** and **Chlorine-37 (37Cl)**, with relative abundances of approximately **75%** and **25%**, respectively.
 
• The atomic mass of chlorine is calculated as the **weighted average of these isotopes**, which results in a fractional value of approximately **35.5 amu** (atomic mass units).
 
• This average is derived using the formula: **(% abundance of isotope 1 × atomic mass of isotope 1) + (% abundance of isotope 2 × atomic mass of isotope 2) / 100**.
 
• Fractional atomic masses are common for elements that have multiple isotopes with varying natural abundances.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chlorine Isotopes:**

 
 
• **Chlorine-35:** This isotope has **17 protons and 18 neutrons**. It constitutes approximately **75%** of natural chlorine.
 
• **Chlorine-37:** This isotope has **17 protons and 20 neutrons**. It accounts for roughly **25%** of natural chlorine.
 
• The slight difference in the number of neutrons between these isotopes is responsible for their different atomic masses.
 
 
 
• **Isotopes and Atomic Mass:**
 
 
• Isotopes have the **same chemical properties** because they have the same number of protons and electrons, which govern chemical behavior.
 
• However, their **physical properties**, such as mass, may differ due to the difference in neutron numbers.
 
• The existence of isotopes is the reason why many elements have **non-integer atomic masses**.
 
 
 
• **How Fractional Atomic Mass is Calculated:**
 
 
• For chlorine:
 
 
• Mass of 35Cl = **34.96885 amu**
 
• Mass of 37Cl = **36.96590 amu**
 
• Weighted average = **(0.75 × 34.96885) + (0.25 × 36.96590) = 35.453 amu**.
 
 
 
• This value is what is reported as the atomic mass of chlorine on the periodic table.
 
 
 
• **Other Elements with Fractional Atomic Masses:**
 
 
• Many elements like **carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen** also exhibit fractional atomic masses due to their isotopic compositions.
 
• For example, the atomic mass of carbon is approximately **12.011 amu** because it has two main isotopes, **Carbon-12** and **Carbon-13**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Options Explained:**

 
 
• **Presence of ions:** Ions are charged particles formed by the loss or gain of electrons. They do not influence the atomic mass of an element. **Incorrect.**
 
• **Experimental error:** Modern techniques ensure precise measurements, so atomic mass values are highly accurate. **Incorrect.**
 
• **Its compound nature:** Compounds are formed by chemical bonds between elements and do not affect the atomic mass of individual atoms. **Incorrect.**

questions.question: Asthma primarily affects which part of the respiratory system?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bronchi and Bronchioles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Asthma** is a chronic respiratory condition that primarily affects the **bronchi and bronchioles**, which are part of the lower respiratory tract.
 
• In asthma, the airways become inflamed, swollen, and constricted, leading to **difficulty in breathing**. This is often triggered by allergens, irritants, or other environmental factors.
 
• During an asthma attack, the muscles surrounding the bronchi and bronchioles tighten, and the airway lining produces excessive mucus, further narrowing the passage for airflow.
 
• The primary symptoms of asthma include **wheezing, shortness of breath, chest tightness**, and coughing, particularly at night or early in the morning.
 
• Asthma is managed using **bronchodilators** (to relax airway muscles) and anti-inflammatory medications (to reduce swelling and prevent symptoms).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Structure and Function of Bronchi and Bronchioles:**

 
 
• The **bronchi** are large air passages branching from the trachea and leading into each lung. They further divide into smaller branches called **bronchioles**.
 
• Bronchi and bronchioles are lined with smooth muscles and mucus-producing cells, which help trap dust and other particles, protecting the lungs.
 
• In asthma, these smooth muscles contract, and the lining becomes swollen, leading to airway narrowing and obstruction.
 
 
 
• **Triggers of Asthma:**
 
 
• Common triggers include pollen, dust mites, pet dander, mold, cold air, exercise, smoke, and respiratory infections.
 
• Other factors like stress, strong emotions, and certain medications can also exacerbate asthma symptoms.
 
 
 
• **Diagnostic Methods:**
 
 
• Asthma is typically diagnosed using a combination of medical history, physical examination, and lung function tests such as **spirometry**.
 
• Spirometry measures the amount and speed of air a person can exhale, helping identify obstructed airways.
 
 
 
• **Treatment Options:**
 
 
• **Quick-relief medications:** Inhaled bronchodilators (e.g., albuterol) provide immediate relief during an asthma attack by relaxing airway muscles.
 
• **Long-term control medications:** Inhaled corticosteroids reduce inflammation in the airways over time, preventing symptoms.
 
• Other treatments include leukotriene modifiers, long-acting beta-agonists (LABAs), and immunotherapy in severe cases.
 
 
 
• **Preventive Measures:**
 
 
• Avoid known triggers like allergens, irritants, and respiratory infections.
 
• Use prescribed medications, such as inhalers, as directed by healthcare professionals.
 
• Maintain a healthy lifestyle, including regular exercise and a balanced diet, to improve lung function and overall health.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Parts of the Respiratory System:**

 
 
• **Trachea:** The windpipe that connects the throat to the bronchi. Asthma does not primarily affect the trachea, although it plays a role in airflow.
 
• **Alveoli:** Tiny air sacs in the lungs where gas exchange occurs. Asthma does not directly affect alveoli but can indirectly impact oxygen exchange due to airflow obstruction.
 
• **Diaphragm:** The main respiratory muscle responsible for breathing. Asthma does not directly affect the diaphragm, but breathing difficulties may result in diaphragm strain.
 
 
 
• **Global Prevalence:**
 
 
• Approximately **262 million people** were affected by asthma globally in **2019**, according to the **World Health Organization (WHO)**.
 
• Asthma is more common in children and is a significant cause of school absenteeism and hospital visits.
 
 
 
• **Economic and Social Impact:**
 
 
• Asthma can lead to reduced productivity, increased healthcare costs, and a lower quality of life if not managed effectively.
 
• Awareness campaigns and affordable access to medications are essential to mitigate its impact, especially in low- and middle-income countries.

questions.question: Which poultry are birds farmed to produce eggs?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Layers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Layers** are a category of poultry birds that are specifically bred and raised for the purpose of producing **eggs**. They are distinct from broilers, which are raised for meat production.
 
• These birds are genetically optimized to lay a high number of eggs, often producing around **250 to 300 eggs** per year under optimal conditions.
 
• Common breeds of layer chickens include **Leghorn, Rhode Island Red, and Sussex**. These breeds are widely used in commercial egg production.
 
• Layer chickens usually start laying eggs at around **18 to 20 weeks** of age and continue to produce eggs efficiently for up to **72 to 80 weeks**.
 
• To maintain high egg production, layers are provided with a balanced diet rich in **calcium, proteins, and essential nutrients**. Proper lighting and temperature control are also critical for their productivity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Broilers:**

 
 
• **Broilers** are poultry birds raised specifically for **meat production**. They are bred to grow quickly and reach market weight in about **6 to 8 weeks**.
 
• Common broiler breeds include **Cornish Cross** and **Plymouth Rock**.
 
• Broilers are not suitable for egg production due to their genetic focus on rapid growth and meat yield.
 
 
 
• **Common Carp:**
 
 
• **Common carp** is a type of fish and not related to poultry. It is extensively farmed for **aquaculture** purposes, primarily for food production.
 
• Carp farming is prevalent in countries like **China** and **India**, where it plays a significant role in meeting the demand for fish.
 
• It has no association with egg production or poultry farming.
 
 
 
• **Milch:**
 
 
• **Milch animals** refer to animals like cows and buffaloes that are raised for **milk production**, not eggs or meat.
 
• Examples include breeds like **Gir, Sahiwal, and Murrah buffalo**.
 
• Milch animals contribute significantly to the dairy industry rather than poultry farming.

questions.question: What happens when a zinc rod is placed in aqueous copper sulphate solution?

options.text: The blue colour of the copper sulphate solution fades.
Heat is required to start the reaction.
The temperature of the solution falls.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The blue colour of the copper sulphate solution fades.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When a **zinc rod** is placed in an **aqueous copper sulphate solution**, a chemical reaction occurs due to the difference in reactivity of zinc and copper.
 
• **Zinc (Zn)** is more reactive than **copper (Cu)** and displaces copper from copper sulphate solution, forming **zinc sulphate (ZnSO₄)**. This process is known as a **displacement reaction.**
 
• The reaction is represented as: **Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu**. Here, zinc replaces copper in the solution, forming zinc sulphate and depositing copper metal.
 
• The fading of the **blue colour** of the copper sulphate solution is due to the formation of **colourless zinc sulphate** in the solution.
 
• This reaction is an example of the reactivity series, where a more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal from its compound. ***Hence, this statement is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Reactivity Series:**

 
 
• The **reactivity series** is a list of metals arranged in order of their reactivity. Zinc is placed higher than copper in the reactivity series, indicating it is more reactive.
 
• Metals higher in the series can displace metals lower in the series from their compounds. For example, **zinc can displace copper**, but copper cannot displace zinc.
 
• This principle is commonly used in various industrial applications, including metal extraction and purification processes.
 
 
 
• **Displacement Reactions:**
 
 
• A **displacement reaction** occurs when a more reactive element replaces a less reactive element in a compound.
 
• Displacement reactions are widely observed in aqueous solutions of salts, such as **copper sulphate**, where reactive metals like zinc or iron displace copper.
 
• Example: **Iron displacing copper** from copper sulphate solution: Fe + CuSO₄ → FeSO₄ + Cu.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of Zinc:**
 
 
• **Zinc** is a metal with atomic number 30 and symbol **Zn**.
 
• It is commonly used in galvanization, alloys, batteries, and chemical reactions due to its high reactivity.
 
• Zinc reacts with acids, bases, and other compounds, often forming salts like zinc sulphate.
 
 
 
• **Copper Sulphate Solution:**
 
 
• **Copper sulphate (CuSO₄)** is a blue-coloured salt used in agriculture (as a fungicide), laboratory experiments, and industry.
 
• In aqueous solutions, copper sulphate dissociates into **Cu²⁺** and **SO₄²⁻** ions, contributing to its characteristic blue colour.
 
• The blue colour fades when copper ions are displaced by zinc or other reactive metals.
 
 
 
• **Applications:**
 
 
• Displacement reactions like this are used in **metal refining**, **electroplating**, and **chemical synthesis**.
 
• The reactivity series helps predict the feasibility of reactions involving metals and their compounds.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
